data.narrative:
Lumaril, a seed-stage robotics and manufacturing company founded by Mark Elliot and Ben Duffield, has raised $12M to date. The relevant comp universe consists of 8 private peers in robotics and manufacturing (including Walden Robotics, Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, and Bedrock Robotics) and 1 public comparable (277810.KQ).

Stage-progression analysis is the primary applicable method given data constraints. Using the $12M total raised as a valuation proxy and applying a 2.5x multiplier typical of seed-to-next-stage advancement yields an implied valuation of $30M. Peer-median triangulation was not applicable; while 8 same-sector peers exist, insufficient datapoints met the filters for same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-tier comparables (minimum threshold: 3 datapoints). Relying on all-sector median without tighter peer alignment would introduce unacceptable noise.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $26M to $34M, with a median of $30M. This range reflects the stage-progression method centered on recent capital deployment. Key uncertainties include: absence of market-derived comparables at the seed stage within robotics and manufacturing, limiting cross-validation of the 2.5x multiplier; and dependency on raised capital as a valuation proxy rather than revenue or unit economics. A fuller triangulation will require additional comparable data or disclosure of operational metrics.
